notes.title: Kunitsu-Gami anniversary update removes Denuvo from Capcom's 9/10 strategy game
notes.notes:
2024 was packed with delights, from the all-conquering Balatro to the bombastic Helldivers 2, and even Elden Ring Shadow of the Erdtree. But Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess was my favorite surprise of the year, a true throwback to developer Capcom's older days and the era of Okami, Onimusha, and Viewtiful Joe. It's just turned one year old, and a special anniversary update includes an 8-bit gift, along with the additional note that it's removed Denuvo anti-tamper.

notes.title: Free update! New extra content, Otherworldly Venture added!
notes.notes:
The extra content, Otherworldly Venture, is a skill-testing mode that emphasizes exhilarating action and strategic thinking.

Set in an alternate world hidden behind the Torii Gate, this new game mode offers a streamlined version of the standard day/night cycle, featuring an endless horde of enemies. The Maiden's health does not regenerate in this mode, so it's game over when her health reaches zero.

Players are challenged to strategically plan positions and villager placements more intensively than in the main game, resulting in a demanding yet rewarding experience.

notes.title: Kunitsu-Gami Path of the Goddess' new mode dials the strategy up to 100
notes.notes:
Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess was my 2024 game of the year. Sure, there was Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree, Dragon Age: The Veilguard, and even Balatro, but Capcom's bizarre tower defense action game hybrid was something new. Developed by Capcom Division 1, the team behind one of my all-time favorite series, Devil May Cry, it's faithfulness to Japanese culture and highly stylized demonic Seethe make it gorgeous to look at, while its hard-as-nails strategy gameplay and slick, almost dance-like combat make it hard but not overly punishing. If you've completed the game already or, like me, want another reason to dive back in, the brand-new Wayward Journey mode is perfect for you - but beware, it's tough as hell.

notes.notes:
Without a shadow of a doubt, one of the most criminally-underrated games of 2024 so far is Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess. While there hasn't been much mainstream chatter about it, and Steam player count numbers have looked fairly underwhelming, I'm happy to see that Capcom's strategic action game has hit a very impressive milestone of 500,000 players. notes.title: Bunraku meets Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess - "Ceremony of the Deity"
notes.notes:
As the launch for Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess draws near, we are announcing a new bunraku (Japanese puppet theatre) play called "Ceremony of the Deity: The Maiden's Destiny" in collaboration with the National Bunraku Theatre. Produced by bunraku artists and supervised by Japan's Living National Treasure, Kanjuro Kiritake, this performance serves as a prequel to the game's narrative.

Discover bunraku, a Japanese culture with a history of over 300 years, through the world of Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess where the puppets for the Maiden and Soh were crafted using traditional techniques. Combined with state-of-the-art technology, the puppets will dance against a CG backdrop of the game's world to evoke a new and enchanting performance. 

Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess launches on Steam on July 19. Demo available to try now.

notes.title: Kunitsu-Gami Path of the Goddess review - truly unique
notes.notes:
As I sit here writing this introduction, I'm at a loss for how to introduce Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess. The brainchild of Capcom Development Division 1, which is responsible for one of my all-time favorite franchises, Devil May Cry, I was worried that this Japanese folklore strategy game turned hack-and-slash adventure would be little more than a fun oddity. Following a brief hands-on at Summer Game Fest, however, I knew that Kunitsu-Gami was something special - something unquantifiable. So, here I am, reviewing a game I hadn't even heard of two months ago, still perplexed as to how to accurately describe what exactly it is.

Read the rest of the story...

A new tale of the Kami awaits…

Introducing Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess: a unique Japanese-inspired,
single player Kagura Action Strategy game. Developed by Capcom, Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess blends intense dancing sword action with strategic gameplay for a unique experience like no other. 

The game takes place on a mountain covered by defilement.
During the day, purify the villages and prepare yourself for sundown.
During the night, protect the Maiden against the hordes of the Seethe.
Repeat the day and night cycle until you cleanse the mountain of defilement and return peace to the land.

Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess is coming to Steam in 2024. Add it to your wishlist now, and let us know what you're most excited to see!
